details:
AstroLink — Explore the Universe Through NASA Data

Project by Team Viper NEX

AstroLink is an interactive NASA Data Explorer designed to make space science, astronomical discoveries, and Earth and planetary research more accessible, understandable, and engaging. It brings NASA's publicly available scientific information into a unified digital platform, allowing users to explore the universe through real scientific data rather than relying solely on static articles or scattered information sources.

The Problem

NASA generates enormous amounts of valuable scientific information through satellites, space missions, telescopes, planetary exploration, and research programs. However, this information is distributed across multiple platforms, APIs, and databases. For students, educators, researchers, and space enthusiasts, discovering relevant information and understanding the connections between different NASA missions can be challenging.

This creates an accessibility gap between the scientific discoveries made by NASA and the people who want to learn about them.

Our Solution

AstroLink addresses this challenge by providing a centralized and interactive environment for exploring NASA's scientific data. The platform is designed to integrate information from 15 NASA APIs, helping users discover and interact with different categories of space-related information through one interface.

Instead of navigating multiple websites and resources, users can access NASA-related information through an organized experience focused on exploration, discovery, and learning.

AstroLink aims to transform complex scientific information into an accessible digital experience that encourages curiosity and makes space exploration more understandable for a wider audience.

Technology and Implementation

AstroLink is developed using modern web technologies, including:

  • React 19: For building an interactive user interface.
  • TypeScript: For maintainable, type-safe application development.
  • Vite: For fast development and optimized production builds.
  • Node.js and Express: For backend services and API communication.
  • Supabase: For database functionality and structured research data storage.
  • Chart.js: For visualizing scientific information.
  • Leaflet: For interactive geographical visualization.
  • Tailwind CSS: For responsive interface design.

The architecture separates frontend presentation, backend services, and database responsibilities. NASA research data is intended to remain database-driven through Supabase rather than being unnecessarily duplicated across application components.

Connection to the Challenge

The NASA Space Apps Challenge theme, "Abandoned but not Forgotten," highlights the scientific legacy of equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

AstroLink provides a broader NASA data exploration environment through which users can discover the scientific context of space missions, understand the importance of planetary exploration, and appreciate the information generated by NASA's research activities.

Our goal is to encourage people to look beyond the equipment itself and understand the scientific knowledge, engineering achievements, and discoveries that these missions have made possible.

Impact and Future Vision

AstroLink aims to make NASA's scientific resources easier to explore for students, educators, researchers, and space enthusiasts. It encourages science education, promotes curiosity about planetary exploration, and demonstrates how technology can connect people with scientific discoveries.

Our long-term vision is to develop AstroLink into a comprehensive space research and discovery platform that makes the universe more accessible through interactive technology, reliable scientific information, and engaging educational experiences.

AstroLink — Connecting People, Science, and the Universe.
